newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Two people killed, two injured in Karachi violence. [CORRECTED 07:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Two people killed, two injured in Karachi violence. [CORRECTED 07:00 GMT]

text.p: Two people were killed and two injured in overnight violence in the troubled Pakistani port city of Karachi, police said on Tuesday.
They said two bodies bearing marks of torture were found in a car in the volatile Orangi area. The victims, one of them a former local councillor, had been strangled.
There was no claim of responsibility and the motive for the killings was not immediately clear.
In a separate incident, Sindh provincial health secretary Shafi Qureshi and his driver were wounded when gunmen fired on their car in Karachi's affluent Clifton area.

At least nine people, including a deputy superintendent of police, have been killed in the past two days of unrest in eastern parts of Karachi, where a small ethnic party has been protesting against the arrest of its workers.
The breakaway Haqiqi faction of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) says police have detained more than 100 of its workers after the killing of a police officer on Friday.
The MQM (corrects name from MQM--Haqiqi) last month renamed itself the Mutahida (united) National Movement to signify the inclusion of groups from outside Karachi's majority Mohajir population.
Mohajirs are Urdu-speaking people who migrated from India at Partition in 1947 and their descendants.
Police said shops in some areas remained shut for the third day running.
Witnesses said police and paramilitary rangers had set up new checkpoints in troubled localities and were patrolling the streets in vehicles mounted with machineguns.
More than 260 people have been killed in political violence in Karachi this year, compared to 500 in 1996 and more than 2,000 in 1995.
